questions.stem:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: The sun
Q: in the east
R: rises
S: every morning
questions.explanation: The correct logical order is Subject + Verb + Place + Time. 'The sun' (P) is the subject, 'rises' (R) is the verb, 'in the east' (Q) is the place, and 'every morning' (S) is the time phrase. Thus, PRQS forms 'The sun rises in the east every morning'.

questions.stem:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: a good boy
Q: Ram
R: is
questions.explanation: The correct grammatical order is Subject + Verb + Complement. 'Ram' (Q) is the subject, 'is' (R) is the linking verb, and 'a good boy' (P) is the subject complement. Thus, QRP forms 'Ram is a good boy'.

questions.stem:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: it is a truth universally acknowledged
Q: must be in want of a wife
R: that a single man in possession of a good fortune
questions.explanation: This is a famous quote. The main clause is 'it is a truth universally acknowledged' (P). The dependent 'that' clause introduces the fact: 'that a single man in possession of a good fortune' (R) followed by the predicate 'must be in want of a wife' (Q). Thus, PRQ.

questions.stem:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: to the bank
Q: he went
R: some money
S: to withdraw
questions.explanation: The main clause is 'He went' (Q). Where did he go? 'to the bank' (P). Why did he go? The infinitive phrase of purpose 'to withdraw' (S) followed by its object 'some money' (R). Thus, QPSR forms 'He went to the bank to withdraw some money'.

questions.stem:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: the old man
Q: of the street
R: across the corner
S: was sitting
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the old man' (P), followed by the verb phrase 'was sitting' (S). The prepositional phrase showing location is 'across the corner' (R), modified by 'of the street' (Q). Thus, PSRQ forms 'The old man was sitting across the corner of the street'.

questions.stem:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: which is the highest peak
Q: Mount Everest
R: is located
S: in the Himalayas
questions.explanation: The main subject is 'Mount Everest' (Q). The relative clause modifying it is 'which is the highest peak' (P). The main verb is 'is located' (R), followed by the prepositional phrase 'in the Himalayas' (S). Thus, QPRS forms 'Mount Everest, which is the highest peak, is located in the Himalayas'.

questions.stem:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: to protect the environment
Q: it is our duty
R: for future generations
S: by reducing pollution
questions.explanation: The main clause is 'it is our duty' (Q). The duty is an infinitive phrase 'to protect the environment' (P). How? 'by reducing pollution' (S). For whom? 'for future generations' (R). Thus, QPSR forms 'It is our duty to protect the environment by reducing pollution for future generations'.

questions.stem: Rearrange sentences P, Q, R, S between the fixed opening (1) and closing (6) to form a coherent paragraph. 1: Reading is among the most rewarding habits one can cultivate. P: A good book introduces new vocabulary and sharpens comprehension over time. Q: It also trains the mind to focus, reducing mental clutter and stress. R: Renowned educators have long urged parents to build reading habits early in children. S: Beyond language, reading broadens one's perspective on culture and human experience. 6: In short, few daily habits offer such a rich return on the time invested. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: P opens with vocabulary and comprehension (language benefit). Q uses 'also' to attach a second benefit of the same reading act, so Q must follow P directly. S says 'Beyond language,' signalling a shift away from the language-skill sentences (P, Q) toward cultural broadening — it must follow both. R (educators' recommendation) is the endorsement that wraps up before sentence 6's summary. Option C places S immediately after P, ignoring that 'Beyond language' presupposes prior language-focused sentences.

questions.stem: Rearrange sentences P, Q, R, S between the fixed opening (1) and closing (6) to form a coherent paragraph. 1: The Sundarbans, shared by India and Bangladesh, is the world's largest tidal mangrove forest. P: This unique ecosystem supports the Bengal tiger, the estuarine crocodile, and hundreds of bird species. Q: Mangrove roots trap sediment, preventing coastal erosion and protecting inland areas from storm surges. R: The forest also sustains thousands of fishing and honey-collecting communities along its margins. S: Climate change and rising sea levels, however, pose an existential threat to this fragile habitat. 6: Conservation efforts spanning both nations are now more urgent than ever before. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: P introduces biodiversity (wildlife). Q describes the ecological service of mangrove roots (structural function). R uses 'also' to add a parallel function — human community sustenance — after Q's ecological service, so R must follow Q. S introduces the threat with 'however,' contrasting the preceding positives, leading naturally into the conservation urgency of sentence 6. Option A places R before Q, breaking the 'also' linkage: R adds to Q's ecological role, not the other way around.

questions.stem: Rearrange sentences P, Q, R, S between the fixed opening (1) and closing (6) to form a coherent paragraph. 1: The Indian independence movement was not a monolithic struggle conducted through a single strategy. P: The moderate faction, led initially by Dadabhai Naoroji, preferred constitutional methods such as petitions and legislative representation. Q: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal, in contrast, championed a more assertive approach rooted in cultural nationalism and mass mobilisation. R: The revolutionary strand, represented by Bhagat Singh and the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, rejected both these paths entirely. S: Gandhi's non-violent civil disobedience ultimately synthesised elements from all camps, creating the broadest possible coalition. 6: This diversity of methods, though sometimes fractious, proved to be the movement's greatest strength. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: The order follows a chronological and logical arc: P (moderates — earliest faction, 1880s) → Q ('in contrast' — extremists emerging as the counter-position to moderates) → R ('both these paths' — revolutionaries explicitly rejecting both P and Q, so R must follow both) → S (Gandhi's synthesis of all three camps). Option B fails because R says 'both these paths,' requiring Q to have already appeared before R can reference it.

questions.stem: Rearrange sentences P, Q, R, S between the fixed opening (1) and closing (6) to form a coherent paragraph. 1: Central banks occupy a unique and indispensable position in any modern economy. P: By setting benchmark interest rates, they influence borrowing costs for commercial banks and, through them, for businesses and households. Q: When inflation threatens to overheat an economy, the central bank typically raises rates to cool aggregate demand. R: Conversely, during recessions, lower rates encourage borrowing and stimulate economic activity significantly. S: In India, the Reserve Bank of India executes this function through its Monetary Policy Committee, which meets six times a year. 6: Understanding these mechanisms is essential for any informed participant in today's economy. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: P establishes the general mechanism (interest rates → borrowing costs). Q applies it to an inflationary scenario (rates rise). R uses 'Conversely' to present the opposite scenario — recession — which must directly follow Q to create the contrast pair. S then narrows the discussion to the Indian institutional example (RBI/MPC), serving as a concrete country-specific illustration after the principle is fully explained. Option C (P → R → Q) violates the 'Conversely' marker: R can only contrast with Q and must therefore follow Q, not precede it.

questions.stem: Rearrange sentences P, Q, R, S between the fixed opening (1) and closing (6) to form a coherent paragraph. 1: The Geographical Indication tag has emerged as a powerful tool for protecting regional heritage products in India. P: A GI tag certifies that a product originates from a specific region and possesses qualities attributable to that geographic origin. Q: Darjeeling tea was the first Indian product to receive a GI tag, setting a landmark precedent in 2004. R: Since then, over 400 products — from Kancheepuram silk to Kolhapuri chappals — have earned this recognition. S: Legal protection under the GI framework prevents manufacturers in other regions from misusing these prestigious names commercially. 6: Critics argue, however, that GI status alone does not guarantee economic uplift for artisans without effective enforcement. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: P defines the GI tag (conceptual foundation — must come first). Q provides the first historical instance (Darjeeling tea, 2004), giving the regime a concrete starting point. R uses 'Since then' to describe expansion since 2004, so R must immediately follow Q. S explains the legal shield afforded by the tag, functioning as the closing functional benefit before the critical counterpoint in sentence 6. Option B places S between P and Q, which severs the essential 'Since then' chronological link between Q and R.

questions.stem: Rearrange sentences P, Q, R, S between the fixed opening (1) and closing (6) to form a coherent paragraph. 1: The doctrine of separation of powers finds a distinctively Indian expression that departs from strict Montesquieuian theory. P: Rather than creating watertight compartments, the Constitution provides for checks and balances through deliberate functional overlaps. Q: Article 74 mandates a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President, subordinating executive authority to elected representatives. R: Simultaneously, judicial independence is safeguarded through security of tenure and the collegium system for judicial appointments. S: The practical tension between legislative sovereignty and judicial review — most visible during constitutional amendments — remains an evolving negotiation. 6: India's model is therefore best described as functional independence coupled with institutional interdependence. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: P establishes India's departure from strict separation (the thesis that overlaps exist). Q illustrates one such overlap — executive subordination to the legislature (Article 74). R uses 'Simultaneously' to present the judicial arm's arrangement as a concurrent, parallel feature, requiring Q to have appeared first. S then synthesises the tension between the two arms discussed in Q and R (legislature vs. judiciary), serving as the analytical conclusion before the summarising label in 6. Option B (P → R → Q) misplaces 'Simultaneously': since R describes an arrangement parallel to Q, Q must precede R.

questions.stem: Rearrange sentences P, Q, R, S between the fixed opening (1) and closing (6) to form a coherent paragraph. 1: The Green Revolution of the 1960s transformed India's agrarian landscape but bequeathed a deeply contested legacy. P: High-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, championed by M.S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug, ended the spectre of recurrent famine within a decade. Q: However, intensive use of chemical fertilisers and groundwater irrigation degraded soil health and caused severe water-table depletion in Punjab and Haryana. R: The benefits also accrued unevenly, bypassing rain-fed regions of eastern India and reinforcing inter-regional economic disparities. S: A second Green Revolution, now being proposed, must therefore reconcile productivity imperatives with ecological sustainability and regional equity. 6: Swaminathan himself, in his later years, became the foremost advocate for precisely this more balanced approach to food security. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: P states the achievement (ending famine) — the positive starting note. Q introduces the environmental downside with 'However,' which must directly counter P's positive claim (so Q follows P). R uses 'also' to append a second limitation (uneven regional benefits) after Q's environmental critique — 'also' signals a second problem, not the first, so R cannot precede Q. S draws the logical prescription with 'therefore,' synthesising solutions to the problems raised in Q and R. Option C (P → R → Q) breaks the logic: 'However' in Q must immediately follow and contrast P, not appear after an intervening sentence.
